title: Tracing fan-out, adaptive alert throttling, and signal-enrichment pipeline
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Background: Our current observability pipeline routes traces to a single hot path for latency SLO evaluation and a separate bulk pipeline for storage. This has led to blind spots during traffic shifts: missing correlated traces for bursty errors, noisy P0 pages from non-actionable signal spikes, and slow downstream enrichment causing delayed alert context.

Goal: Implement a tracing fan-out and signal-enrichment layer that: 1) replicates a lightweight trace stream to SLO/eval consumers, anomaly detectors, and short-term hot stores; 2) performs realtime enrichment (user context, route tags, model variant) so alerts have actionable links; and 3) applies adaptive alert throttling (per-route backoff + temporary suppression with burn-like rate decay) to reduce pager noise while preserving detection of true incidents.

Scope:
- Add a low-latency fan-out service that subscribes to the existing jaeger/beeline collector output and emits three parallel streams: quick-path SLO consumer, anomaly-detector, and bulk-archive.
- Enrichment functions to attach tokenized prompt hash, model variant, customer_id (where allowed by policy), and trace-level sampling state.
- Implement adaptive throttling policy: when paging for a given SLO route exceeds a noise threshold, switch to exponential suppression windows (small initial suppressions for low-severity blips, longer windows during noisy storms). This is intentionally different from the previous global burn-rate approach — it is route-aware and preserves higher-fidelity sampling for routes that remain critical.
- Provide observable metrics for fan-out lag, enrichment latency (p95/p99), suppression windows, and lost-samples rate.

Non-goals: full rework of storage tiering, changes to SLO definitions, or migrating legacy dashboards in this ticket.

Success criteria:
- 95% of SLO-triggered traces delivered to SLO consumers within 2s (p95) and 5s (p99).
- Pager volume for repeat noisy routes reduced by >= 60% in first-week post-deploy without missing confirmed incidents.
- Enriched alerts include trace link and model-variant tag >= 98% of the time for non-sampled traces.
comments: 2026-03-03 - Kickoff: Aligning ENG, SRE, and PM on scope. Priya and Leo sketched fan-out topology and agreed enrichment fields. Action: prototype small fan-out using kafka topic + consumer group shim.

2026-03-05 - Prototype: PoC fan-out created (kafka fanout consumer). Observed average extra latency +40ms; p99 spikes up to 1.2s due to synchronous enrichment lookup. Decided to make enrichment async with best-effort attach when feasible.

2026-03-07 - Design review: Discussed adaptive throttling policy. SRE requested route-weighted suppression rather than global burn-rate. PM requested telemetry hooks for rollback. Recorded notes in design doc: https://confluence.redwood/intern/obs/fanout-enrichment (internal).

2026-03-09 - Security review: Confirmed customer_id enrichment requires masking for private deployments. Added feature flag and KMS gating for PII. Security: @Janelle awarded conditional approval; complete review pending for private package. (See PR comment).

2026-03-11 - Implementation: Began implementation of suppression engine. Unit tests for exponential backoff logic added. Initial dashboard widget created: /grafana/d/obs/fanout-health showing fanout-lag and enrichment-latency. Link to WIP PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs/pull/2124

2026-03-12 - Early Canary: Deployed fan-out to canary (10% traffic) for runtime-1.22. Observed suppressed pages on three noisy internal routes; incident routing preserved for high-severity alerts. Need to tune suppression thresholds — they are currently conservative.

2026-03-13 - PM feedback: Add 'sample-preserve' mode for routes that need full trace capture for auditing. PM requested a small UI toggle in Console rollouts for teams to opt-in. Logged follow-up: ENG-18305 (Console toggle).
next_steps: finish async enrichment worker and add cache for model-variant lookup
tune suppression thresholds with SRE and run 72h canary
add Console toggle task (ENG-18305) and privacy gating for private deployments
notes: Trade-off: fully synchronous enrichment simplifies alert context but harms p99 latency — chosen to favor async best-effort enrichment with a small synchronous critical-path set (trace_id, route_id).
Fallback plan: if fan-out causes >2x p99 regression in canary, revert fan-out consumer and keep enrichment worker disabled until optimized.
